lead: walk through your own flat and there is nothing in it your hands made; it all went out the week it was finished, and no second part of you stayed behind to keep a list.
sun: people do not experience being given anything by you. there is no moment with an edge on it, no pause where a thing changes hands, so what starts at your table arrives in somebody's week already theirs, already running, indistinguishable from a decision they made. ask where it began and they name themselves, honestly, and they are not being greedy about it. nothing happened that anybody could have witnessed.
moon: the reaching and the letting go are the same movement in here, so a thing is never yours for the interval in which you could feel it as yours. no version of you holds it up to the light first. what other people call generosity has a moment in it where they decide, and that moment is missing at both ends of you.
pull: you have made more than anyone you know and cannot produce one item of evidence. the second copy — the one that stays home and keeps count — was never in you.
tension: the trouble arrives as a plain question — what has all of it added up to. somebody who has watched a decade of it wants a number, and you do not have one, and not having one sounds exactly like refusing to give it. you could assemble the total and you are the one party with no record, so the argument closes with you agreeing to a version of your life you have no means of checking.
cost: things get out of your hands and into the world at a rate nobody around you can match, and none of it drags: no conditions, no follow-up, no version where you check how it is going. every year of it is real and every year of it is gone, and if the whole of it were taken off you tomorrow there would be nothing to show the difference against.

lead: one thing in your life carries your name. it is the smallest thing you have made, it is the only part of you a stranger can find, and every person who comes to you comes through it.
sun: the named object brings people to you; the unnamed one is what they leave with. somebody arrives having admired a single item, sits down for an hour, and goes home with a plan and a way of working that did not exist before they walked in. what they can name afterwards is the item, so the item takes the whole account, and the hour goes down as a good conversation.
moon: an item that visible attracts handling, and nothing in you stands over it. that would survive if there were a body of work behind it, and behind it there is motion running in other people under their names, none of it available as evidence. so the single piece anybody can attribute to you is the single piece anybody can take, and taking it leaves the record blank.
pull: the one thing with your name on it brought them all here. what they left with was made after they arrived, and it carries nothing.
tension: the people working inside things you started will tell you, without malice, that you did one good thing early and have been coasting since. they cannot connect the two, because nothing connects them. correcting it means walking into somebody's career and claiming a share of it out loud, on no evidence but your own memory — so the sentence stands, and the one item on the record keeps getting smaller as the years put distance behind it.
cost: an admirer walks in and walks out changed, equipped, with something of their own to build, and you do that without needing any part of it back. the record of you is one object. defending it is the only defence available, so a lifetime of untraceable output stands or falls on how a single visible thing is treated by people who did not make it.

lead: the form wants a title and the name of a place, and both boxes have been guesses for twenty years. everything you have actually done is somewhere else, held in pieces by people who have never met.
sun: what you start needs an address to come back to, and you have not held one. the motion goes out, it does well, and the gratitude arrives at whatever position you occupied that year — a project since closed, a room you were passing through, a name on a door that has been repainted twice. so the thanks and the referrals go to the last known location and stop there.
moon: nothing in you arranged this. you have never declined to stay next to a thing; the question has never arrived — you are already elsewhere by the time it has a shape people can gather around. the ones who keep asking where you are based are not being nosy. they are trying to work out how to introduce you.
pull: nothing about you can be looked up. what you have made runs under other names and where you belong is filed nowhere, so the sum of you exists as things other people are doing.
tension: a person who cannot say what they do gets read as either unserious or as covering something. both readings get made about you, usually kindly, and there is no third one available. the people who could correct it each hold one fragment and have never met, so the only complete account of you would have to be assembled by you, out of memory, in a room where saying it aloud sounds like a claim.
cost: you can begin something in a room where you have no standing, which is normally the one thing that stops a person — no post to protect, nothing that has to be squared first. the accumulation never happens. thirty years of starts leave no position, no institution that would claim you, and no line of the kind that gets you into rooms you have not already talked your way into.

lead: they are winning with an argument that was yours first — you handed it over in a car park eighteen months ago, before any of this, and by now it belongs to them in every way anybody could check.
sun: you make with whoever is in front of you, and that includes the person across the table in a dispute. an hour with them and something exists that did not — a way through, a phrase that clarifies their position — and it left your hands at the moment it was said. it is running on their side now, under their name, and nothing at your end can call it back.
moon: both cases are live in here at full weight, and neither is a doubt about the other. so the fight does not narrow you the way a fight is supposed to: you go on seeing exactly what would strengthen their side, in detail, the same way you see your own, and seeing it is already halfway to building it.
pull: both sides of this fight are running on things you made. what you handed the other one cannot be traced, cannot be claimed, and came back at you this week in their words.
tension: your side has noticed that you still take their calls. it gets described as going soft, and sharply as playing both ends, and the sharper version is nearer the mark — something useful crosses every time you speak. defending it means saying the sentence nobody on your side can hear: that the fight is better when their case is at its best. in the week of a hearing that sounds like a person who has already gone over.
cost: nobody comes out of a fight with you stupider than they went in, and the thing itself stays the subject long after most disputes have turned personal. you have never carried one outright. every strong move the other side has made this decade was made by somebody who spent an hour with you, and the total of those hours is unknown to them and unavailable to you.
